core_obligations: Independence of the factorizations: given two factorizations a_1 = u_1 pi^{e_1} = v_1 theta^{f_1} and a_2 = u_2 pi^{e_2} = v_2 theta^{f_2} in a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring, derive a_1^{e_2} = u_1^{e_2} u_2^{-e_1} a_2^{e_1} and the analogous theta-relation, set m = length_B(B/pi B) and k = length_B(B/theta B), use length_B(B/a_2B) to get e_2 m = f_2 k, and expand a_1^{e_2 m} = a_1^{f_2 k} to obtain (u_1^{e_2}u_2^{-e_1})^m = (v_1^{f_2}v_2^{-f_1})^k; the sign is then settled by showing me_1e_2 and kf_1f_2 have the same parity (proof lines 838-861).

Independence of the extension: for two extensions A contained in B and A contained in B' as in the preparation lemma, form C = (B tensor_A B')/(m-power torsion), which is a third admissible extension; after replacing by A contained in B contained in C one may use transitivity of norms, which reduces the claim to the numerical identity lambda^m = prod Norm_{kappa_k/kappa}(lambda)^{m_k} for a nonzerodivisor pi in a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring B and the maximal ideals m_k of C (proof lines 864-893).

Prove the numerical identity: Norm_{kappa_k/kappa}(lambda) = lambda^{[kappa_k:kappa]} since lambda lies in kappa, and m = length_B(B/pi B) = length_B(C/pi C) = sum m_k [kappa_k : kappa], the first equality by the comparison lemma and the defining equation of e_R, the second by the pushdown lemma for modules (proof lines 891-898).
proof_roadmap: Prove independence of the factorization: convert the two factorizations into unit identities by clearing powers, compare the multiplicities e_2 m = f_2 k, and settle the sign by a parity argument (proof lines 838-861).
Reduce independence of the extension to a norm identity: build the third extension C, use transitivity of norms, and reduce to lambda^m = prod Norm(lambda)^{m_k} (proof lines 864-893).

Verify the norm identity by computing both sides: the norms are powers of lambda by the degree, and the exponents add up by the length comparison lemma together with the pushdown lemma (proof lines 891-898).
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes that the displayed formula for the tame symbol gives a well-defined element of kappa(m)*, i.e. that the right-hand side is independent both of the local factorizations chosen and of the admissible extension B (statement lines 831-834). The two independence statements are proved by genuinely different arguments: the first turns the two factorizations into a unit identity by clearing powers and then settles the sign through a parity check on the exponents, while the second builds a third extension C dominating both, invokes transitivity of norms, and reduces everything to the numerical identity lambda^m = prod Norm(lambda)^{m_k}, which is then verified by comparing lengths using the comparison lemma and the pushdown lemma (proof lines 838-898). What is not routine is the bookkeeping that makes lambda^m match the product of the norms, in particular the identity m = sum m_k [kappa_k : kappa]. The claim is H2.
